summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a complex medical history including acute myeloid leukemia in remission, chronic graft-versus-host disease, systolic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, chronic kidney disease, and recent perirectal abscess treated with incision and drainage, was admitted for acute-onset worsening diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting. He had been discharged from rehabilitation the day prior. Stool testing confirmed Clostridioides difficile infection, and he was started on oral vancomycin. His symptoms improved significantly over the hospital stay, with bowel movements decreasing to one or two per day by discharge. His heart failure remained stable, potassium normalized, and platelet count was monitored for a mild downtrend possibly related to medication. He was discharged to an extended care rehabilitation facility to continue physical therapy and complete his antibiotic course, with instructions to monitor for recurrence of diarrhea, weight gain, or other complications.
